source.title: JPU: Bridging Jailbreak Defense and Unlearning via On-Policy Path Rectification
source.authors: Xi Wang; Songlei Jian; Shasha Li; Xiaopeng Li; Zhaoye Li; Bin Ji; Baosheng Wang; Jie Yu

record.file_problem: The paper text is present through its conclusion, limitations, appendices, and algorithm. Some table layout is flattened, so the attack-column mapping is unclear.
record.tranche_reason: It evaluates unlearning and a new defense against jailbreak prompts and analyzes internal activation/path behavior, but it does not test the specified fine-tuning, ablation, or quantization recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The study reports jailbreak attack success rates (ASR) for unlearning defenses and JPU, plus its own internal-path analyses. Table 1 has eight values per model and method, but the flattened header does not reliably associate those positions with named attacks or datasets; rows therefore identify positions rather than guessing mappings. Results cited from earlier work and values used only for design choices are not recorded as findings.
record.test_reason: The paper studies jailbreak defense. Its unlearning baselines (Eraser, Safe Unlearning, CKU) and JPU suppress harmful compliance; none removes a targeted knowledge set. The measure is jailbreak attack success rate (ASR) against the base model under the same attack. No targeted-knowledge accuracy is reported, and there is no ASR for the unlearned model without attack, so no row shows knowledge recovered after unlearning. The internal-path analysis (Fig 1, Fig 3) uses the 'unlearning leaves paths' idea to motivate JPU. It is qualitative or figure-only and concerns refusal behaviour rather than erased knowledge. The paper mainly reports its own method's performance.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. Authors conclude static unlearning defenses leave dynamic jailbreak paths through non-erased intermediate-layer parameters. They say JPU rectifies these paths, giving lower ASR in nearly all settings while preserving utility.
record.recipe_differences: JPU uses on-policy attack-buffer mining, path identification, and constrained path rectification rather than the claim’s recovery attacks; the study also evaluates Eraser, Safe Unlearning, and CKU as defenses.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model and table condition. The paper also reports sensitivity to layer selection and path sparsity; shallow and middle-layer variants defend less effectively than the full strategy.

fits_no_version.finding: Jailbreaks still elicit harmful outputs from unlearning-based jailbreak defenses. Examples: Eraser on Llama-2 at 17.27% ASR under AutoDAN/AdvE (base 27.10); CKU at 14.10% under MIX-JAIL on Llama-3 (base 16.43). Qualitative SNIP and IGI analysis says jailbreaks route through non-erased intermediate-layer parameters.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning-based safety (refusal) defenses leave residual jailbreak vulnerability via non-erased internal paths.

fits_no_version.finding: A path-rectifying unlearning method (JPU) lowers jailbreak ASR below other unlearning defenses in most settings. Reported ASRs include 0.00–12.20%, and Llama-2 MIX-JAIL falls to 4.44 vs CKU 8.15. Utility is preserved.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Path-level unlearning improves jailbreak robustness over parameter-level unlearning.

record.problems: Table 1's flattened header prevents reliable assignment of its eight values to named attack/dataset conditions. No uncertainty estimates are reported. ASR is not a direct targeted-knowledge accuracy or recovery measure, and the paper does not compare to a model that never possessed the target knowledge.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 includes other comparison methods (RSFT and Circuit Breaker), whose results are not included here because they are not unlearning methods at issue in this claim. No other claim-relevant numbered result was omitted.

untested.parts: No targeted-knowledge accuracy, near-chance check or knowledge-recovery attack.
No direction ablation; path analysis is qualitative and about refusal circuitry, not erased knowledge.
Jailbreak ASR only, with no unlearned-no-attack baseline and no knowledge measure.
JPU is evaluated only on prompt and decoding jailbreak ASR. There are no relearning, ablation or quantization attacks, and no knowledge measure.

record.verdict_notes: Unlearning here targets harmful compliance (refusal training), not a knowledge set like WMDP or Harry Potter, and the study is not among the original sources. The flattened Table 1 header can be mapped by order: AIM(AdvB, AdvE), GCG(AdvB, AdvE), AutoDAN(AdvB, AdvE), Decoding(MaliciousInstruct), MIX-JAIL(AdvB-Short). No uncertainty is reported, and the paper is a preprint.

versions.untested_parts: No targeted-knowledge accuracy or near-chance measure is reported after unlearning. The paper reports utility and jailbreak ASR, not whether targeted knowledge accuracy reaches near chance.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack is tested.
No ablation of an activation direction is tested; the relevant evidence is the paper’s analysis of activation overlap and jailbreak paths.
No low-bit quantization attack is tested.

The study tests jailbreak prompts, but not recovery by other languages, in-context information, or prompt rephrasing as separate conditions. It reports harmful-output ASR rather than recovery of targeted-knowledge accuracy.
JPU is evaluated against jailbreak prompts, but not against fine-tuning, activation ablation, or quantization recovery attacks.

rows.subject: erased LLM (Lu et al., 2024)
rows.operation_detail: Compared activated-parameter overlap for successful jailbreak queries and standard harmful queries using SNIP importance analysis.

conditions.value: successful jailbreak queries vs. standard harmful queries

rows.value: The paper describes the overlap as minimal.
rows.note: The authors interpret this as jailbreaks activating parameters outside the regions associated with harmful queries; no numeric overlap value is given.
rows.check: Qualitative SNIP overlap claim ('minimal overlap') about harmful-query vs jailbreak parameters in Eraser. No number, and it concerns refusal or harmful-compliance circuitry, not erased knowledge. Belongs in fits_no_version.

rows.subject: erased LLM (Lu et al., 2024)
rows.operation_detail: Traced alignment between jailbreak-induced paths and direct-harm trajectories using Inter-layer Gradient Integration.

conditions.value: diverse jailbreak paths vs. direct-harm trajectories

rows.value: The paper states that jailbreak paths progressively converge with harmful pathways toward the final layers and unsafe outputs.
rows.note: No numeric path-alignment value is stated.
rows.check: Illustrative Fig 1(b) path-convergence claim with no number. Same construct mismatch as r1.

rows.subject: Llama-2-Erased
rows.operation_detail: Compared layer-wise jailbreak/harmful-path overlap for the baseline against JPU.
rows.uncertainty: Variability across attack methods is shown as shaded regions; numeric uncertainty is not stated.
rows.note: The text says JPU consistently reduces path overlap across critical layers; the plotted values are not transcribed as numbers.
rows.check: Fig 3 compares the study's own method (JPU) with Eraser on path IoU. This is an own-method comparison, figure only.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Eraser, Safe Unlearning, and CKU on the evaluated jailbreak conditions in Table 1
reader_labels.reason: Jailbreak ASR remains nonzero in nearly all reported conditions, but is generally below the base-model ASR; these results show incomplete attack vulnerability rather than broad restoration of targeted knowledge (r4-r51).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: The paper’s analysis of the erased LLM
reader_labels.reason: The authors report minimal overlap with harmful-query parameters and convergence of jailbreak paths toward harmful trajectories, consistent with persistent access paths (r1-r2).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: JPU on the reported Table 1 conditions
reader_labels.reason: JPU has lower ASR than the base model across the reported positions and the authors report the best ASR in nearly all settings (r52-r56, r58-r60).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: JPU conditions with residual ASR and the tested attack scope
reader_labels.reason: Some JPU conditions retain nontrivial ASR, and the evaluation does not test the fine-tuning, internal-ablation, or quantization attacks named in the broader claim (r57).
